open_points.subject: repeatability of function execution
open_points.text: Rule 3 says code depending on module-loading facts “may answer differently between releases and between executions”, while required test 6 says “The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.”
open_points.question: Must equal implementation and input produce equal output despite dependence on unspecified module-loading metadata, or is such execution-to-execution variation permitted?
options: Require equal output digests for every repeated execution.
Permit different outputs when code observes unspecified loading metadata.
Exclude metadata-dependent implementations from the repeatability guarantee, with a defined way to identify them.
open_points.default_guess: Permit the variation because the changed normative rule explicitly allows it, and narrow or remove the repeatability test.

witness.initial: A contract has one string output and a trial case with fixed inputs; its implementation returns getattr(sys.modules[__name__], '__file__', '').
events: The kernel executes the implementation once using a temporary module path.
The kernel executes the same implementation again with the same input using another fresh sandbox and another permissible module path.
outcomes: Both executions must have the same output digest under required test 6.
The executions may return different paths and therefore different output digests under changed rule 3.
witness.observer: The agent reading the two TrialExecutions, and admission if an expected output is present.

open_points.subject: deterministic admission verdict
open_points.text: M08 and K-05 call admission “the deterministic verdict” for an implementation and corpus, while changed A03 rule 3 permits code observing unspecified loading metadata to “answer differently between releases and between executions”.
open_points.question: Is an AdmissionVerdict required to be reproducible from only the implementation and corpus, and if so how are implementations that observe unspecified module-loading facts handled?
options: Admission must be reproducible, so all observable loading facts must be fixed.
Admission may differ between executions or conforming kernels when code observes unspecified loading facts.
Such code must receive a specified failing outcome before its outputs affect admission.
open_points.default_guess: Treat admission as deterministic only after fixing the concrete execution observations, allowing metadata-dependent submissions to receive different verdicts on fresh admissions.

witness.initial: A contract has one string output; its corpus expects a particular path string; the implementation returns its module's __file__.
events: An agent submits the implementation and admission runs in a conforming kernel whose loader uses the expected path.
outcomes: A loader fixing that permitted path produces a passing case and an admitted verdict.
A loader using another permitted path produces output_mismatch and a refused verdict.
witness.observer: The submitting agent, and callers that see whether the implementation became active.

open_points.subject: module file timestamps as a function time source
open_points.text: Changed A03 rule 3 says a module file's timestamps are not fixed and code depending on them may answer differently, while A19 rule 4 says “Functions have no clock (A03)” and K-02 requires “no clock”.
open_points.question: May function code observe real or execution-varying timestamps through its module file metadata, or must those timestamps be unavailable or deterministic to preserve the no-clock rule?
options: Expose actual loader-file timestamps as unspecified observable metadata.
Give module files fixed deterministic timestamps.
Make timestamp inspection unavailable to function code.
open_points.default_guess: Allow the unspecified timestamps because the newer A03 text expressly permits dependence on them, treating “no clock” as only forbidding current-time APIs.

witness.initial: An implementation returns os.stat(sys.modules[__name__].__file__).st_mtime_ns through an integer output port.
events: The implementation is executed in two fresh sandboxes created at different times.
outcomes: Under the no-clock rule, both executions expose no changing time source, through fixed metadata or a failure.
Under changed A03 rule 3, each execution may expose its loader file's different timestamp and succeed with a different value.
witness.observer: The agent reading trial outputs or a flow output.

open_points.subject: validation pipeline for MCP discovery methods
open_points.text: Rule 1 says every request must name a known operation and fit that operation's schema, and rule 4 says “Every request is validated against its schema”; changed rule 3 says initialize, ping and tools/list “name no operation” and any known token gets their answer after the size, token and depth checks.
open_points.question: After size, token and depth checks, are discovery requests schema-validated, and what happens when they contain unknown or malformed fields?
options: Discovery methods bypass operation lookup and schema validation and answer regardless of remaining fields.
Each discovery method has its own request schema, validated at the normal schema step.
They are rejected because they name no catalogue operation, except for a separately specified special-case request shape.
open_points.default_guess: Give each discovery method its own schema and validate it after depth, while exempting it only from the actor-action table and catalogue-operation lookup.

witness.initial: The caller has a known agent token and the kernel is serving normally.
events: The caller sends tools/list within the size and depth limits but includes an unknown parameter.
outcomes: Changed rule 3 is read as an exception after the named three checks, so the kernel returns the catalogue.
Rules 1 and 4 are applied to every request, so the kernel returns invalid_request for the unknown field.
